title: Refactor heterogeneous tenant references to a single canonical tenant_id and introduce zero-downtime FK enforcement
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several control-plane tables use different columns and types to represent tenant/owner identity (tenant_id text, tenant_uuid uuid, owner integer, acct_key varchar). This inconsistency prevents foreign key enforcement, increases join cost, complicates permissions logic, and causes subtle bugs during multi-tenant queries. The goal of this ticket is to introduce a single canonical column tenant_id (bigint), backfill and migrate existing references with zero-downtime, add FK constraints on critical hot tables, and then deprecate legacy columns after a probation window.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical tenant_id bigint column exists on all core control-plane tables required by platform reads and writes.
Background migration completes for >99.9% of rows with verified mapping accuracy (checksum-based validation).
FK constraints added to high-read tables (control_events, deployments, project_ownership) without causing >2x latency on hot read queries during rollout.
Compatibility layer (views or DB-level generated columns) provided for older services, enabling a 4-week deprecation window before removing legacy columns.
Monitoring dashboards show no customer-facing errors or SLO violations attributable to this migration during rollout.
Cleanup task scheduled to remove legacy columns and tighten indexes after the deprecation window.
Automated test coverage exists for dual-write, fallback path, and backfill idempotency jobs.
migration_strategy: 1) Add nullable canonical column tenant_id (bigint) to each table, no default.
2) Implement service-side dual-write: new code paths write both legacy columns and canonical tenant_id behind a feature flag (no immediate switch).
3) Backfill tenant_id in small chunks using a leader job that reads legacy values, maps them to canonical ids via tenant_lookup table, and writes tenant_id with minimal locking.
4) Run verification job to checksum between legacy joins and canonical joins for a sample of hot queries.
5) After verification and monitoring for 72h, add FK constraints and targeted partial indexes on hot predicates with CONCURRENTLY where supported.
6) Flip feature flags to read from canonical tenant_id, still writing legacy columns for safety.
7) Deprecation window (4 weeks) with rollback capability: turn feature flag back to legacy reads if issues observed.
8) Remove legacy columns in a controlled maintenance window once stable and archive old values in audit table.
rollout_plan: Canary: pick two low-traffic internal orgs and run the full backfill and read switch while monitoring SLOs.
Gradual: scale canary to 10% of production traffic; validate metrics (p95 latency, DB CPU, index bloat).
Full: after 7 days at 10% with no regressions, roll out to remaining tenants in 3 waves using region-aware batching.
Post-rollout: schedule cleanup job and tag removal PR for release-2 weeks after canary success.
rollback_plan: If checksum mismatch >0.1% or p95 latency spike >1.5x, pause backfill and revert reads to legacy columns by toggling feature flag.
If FK add fails with locks longer than 30s on any hot table, abort and switch to creating a supporting partial index first to reduce lock contention.
Keep dual-write active for 2 weeks after rollback to allow manual reconciliation jobs.
monitoring_queries: select count(*) from control_events where tenant_id is null;
compare: select count(*) from control_events join tenants on control_events.tenant_id = tenants.id vs select count(*) using legacy mapping
db: track pg_stat_activity waiting_locks during CONCURRENTLY index/constraint adds
app: error rate per tenant (5xx) and p95 request latency for control-plane routes that join on tenant fields
notes: Trade-offs discussed: introducing a bigint canonical id requires mapping from existing uuids/strings; mapping table (tenant_lookup) must be authoritative and kept small.
We considered keeping tenant as a uuid everywhere but chose bigint for index compactness and consistent join performance.
Locking risk: adding FK on huge tables must be done with CONCURRENTLY where possible, or via creating supporting index prior to constraint to reduce lock time.
We will coordinate with SRE to increase DB maintenance connection limits during the CONCURRENTLY operations.
blockers: Need a tenant_lookup canonicalization script verified by product to map legacy tenant keys (PM sign-off).
Backfill job needs a dedicated low-priority worker queue to avoid starving online workers (infra quota request pending).
decisions: Use bigint canonical tenant_id instead of uuid - decided 2025-02-14 after perf bench comparing index size and join throughput (see bench notes).
Dual-write approach chosen to avoid a big-bang switch and allow incremental verification.
FK enforcement will be incremental: only add to critical read-heavy tables first (control_events, deployments, project_ownership) and then expand.
